gate: Phase A.6 Harness Gate -- BLOCKING, equal weight to the Context Delivery Plan gate (ORCHESTRATION_TEMPLATE.md STEP 10 / phase-A.6.md)

consulted.harness_mathematics_expert: Little's Law throughput bounds, Wilson-CI/E[attempts] story-level circuit-breaker derivation, Clopper-Pearson transient-retry derivation, capped-exponential-with-full-jitter backoff derivation -- all consumed verbatim below, not re-derived here

retroactive_gap_disclosure.status: ACTIVATED RETROACTIVELY -- disclosed gap, not backdated
retroactive_gap_disclosure.what_happened: Phase A.6/A.6.1 harness gate is being produced and committed now (2026-09-19), after Phase B (Waves 2-5 implementation, 38 agents / 12,479,018 tokens / 0 errors) and the P1 remediation workflow (26 agents / 6,990,891 tokens / 0 errors, 2 of 4 stories needed a 2nd attempt) had already run to completion without this policy existing as a committed artifact.
retroactive_gap_disclosure.why_disclosed_here: ORCHESTRATION_TEMPLATE.md STEP 10 states harness_control_policy.json must be committed BEFORE any Phase B agent receives its prompt (BLOCKING gate). That did not happen for Waves 2-5 or the P1 remediation run. This field records that fact plainly instead of silently backdating the artifact's effective date to precede the work it did not actually govern.
retroactive_gap_disclosure.scope_of_applicability: This policy governs Phase B / P1-remediation-class work FROM THIS COMMIT FORWARD. It does not retroactively validate or invalidate the already-completed Waves 2-5 or P1 remediation runs -- those are grounded empirically (see empirical_grounding below) as the DATA this policy's thresholds were derived FROM, not as runs that were compliant WITH a policy that did not yet exist.
retroactive_gap_disclosure.dispatch_mechanism_caveat: This project's actual dispatch mechanism is the Claude Code Workflow/Agent tools (Task-style subagent spawns), not a literal prompt-injection orchestrator-agent runtime that mechanically prepends this JSON as a header block to every subagent prompt. Consequently, enforcement of this policy going forward is SELF-APPLIED by whichever agent (orchestrator persona or the coordinating session) dispatches each future Task/Agent call -- the coordinating agent is responsible for reading this policy and honoring its stop conditions, budgets, retry/backoff, and circuit-breaker rules at each dispatch, rather than the harness mechanically injecting and enforcing it outside the dispatching agent's control.

waves_2_5_workflow.note: tokens_per_story_approx = total_tokens / stories-covered in this wave set; cited as one of the two cross-phase inputs to the per-story-group ceiling derivation

p1_remediation_workflow.note: tokens_per_story_attempt_approx is the higher of the two cross-phase per-story token figures and is the binding input to the per-story-group ceiling derivation

transient_call_reliability_sample.note: 0/64 observed transient tool-dispatch failures across the two workflows above; feeds the Clopper-Pearson upper-bound derivation for the transient-retry layer, NOT the story-level circuit breaker

stop_conditions.description: The disjunctive stop predicate governing any single agent-loop run dispatched under this policy (per agent-loop-lifecycle-core / stop-condition-budget-control-core). All four disjuncts are mandatory; a run halts the instant any one fires.

disjuncts.name: natural_final
disjuncts.trigger: agent emits a final answer with no further tool calls

disjuncts.name: max_turn_cap
disjuncts.trigger: turn >= T_max for the dispatched agent
disjuncts.note: T_max is set per-agent-role in the Context Delivery Plan; this policy does not override per-role T_max values, it enforces that one is always set (no unbounded loop is permitted, per agent-loop-lifecycle-core Operating Rule)

disjuncts.name: budget_guard
disjuncts.trigger: cumulative tokens for the run >= per-agent ceiling (see token_budget_ceilings below)

disjuncts.name: output_contract_check
disjuncts.trigger: agent's final output fails the phase's required artifact schema/contract (e.g. does not match the expected JSON schema for its phase deliverable)

stop_conditions.convergence_signal: for Fix->QA->Review->P1 remediation loops specifically, convergence is a distinct concept from the four disjuncts above -- see circuit_breakers.story_level_loop_breaker; a converged (APPROVED) verdict is a natural_final exit at the STORY level, composed from possibly several agent-loop runs underneath

token_budget_ceilings.derivation_summary: tau_bar + 2 standard deviations on tokens/story-attempt (per-agent ceiling) and tokens/story cross-phase agreement (per-story-group ceiling), computed by harness-mathematics-expert against the empirical_grounding figures above. Per-agent ceiling divides the per-story-attempt tau_bar+2s figure by a conservative agents-per-story ratio observed across both workflows.
token_budget_ceilings.per_agent_ceiling_margin_note: ~18-23% margin over the observed mean tokens/agent across Waves 2-5 (38 agents / 12,479,018 tokens = ~328,395 mean) and P1 remediation (26 agents / 6,990,891 tokens = ~268,880 mean)
token_budget_ceilings.per_story_group_ceiling_margin_note: ~9% margin over the higher of the two observed cross-phase figures: 1,134,456 tokens/story (Waves 2-5) vs 1,165,149 tokens/story-attempt (P1 remediation) -- ceiling is set against the higher (P1 remediation) figure
token_budget_ceilings.enforcement: cumulative tokens for a single dispatched agent >= per_agent_ceiling_tokens fires the budget_guard stop condition for that agent; cumulative tokens for all agents working a single story (across its full Fix->QA->Review->P1 loop) >= per_story_group_ceiling_tokens fires an ESCALATE recommendation to the coordinating session, independent of the story-level circuit breaker's attempt count

two_distinct_levers.rate_limit_note: this policy specifies budget (cumulative/stock) ceilings only; instantaneous rate-limit (token-bucket burst) governance is out of scope for this artifact and is deferred to the provider-level rate limits already in force for the Claude Code / Agent SDK dispatch mechanism -- see dispatch_mechanism_caveat above for why no separate token-bucket is implemented at the harness layer in this project
two_distinct_levers.budget_limit: governed by per_agent_ceiling_tokens and per_story_group_ceiling_tokens above; hard stop, no recovery within the run

retry_backoff_schedule.description: Transient agent-call / tool-dispatch retry layer. DISTINCT from the story-level circuit breaker below -- this layer handles a dropped, errored, or rate-limited tool/agent DISPATCH (a transport-level failure), not a review-quality rejection (Fix->QA->Review verdict of REJECTED, which is handled by the story-level breaker).
retry_backoff_schedule.derivation_summary: k=3 total attempts derived from Clopper-Pearson exact upper confidence bound p_upper=4.57% at 0/64 observed transient-call failures (empirical_grounding.transient_call_reliability_sample). Backoff schedule derived per retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M1/M2 general form delay(n)=min(cap, base*2^n) with full jitter.
non_retryable_error_classes: review-quality REJECTED verdict (handled by story-level breaker, not this layer)
retry_backoff_schedule.jitter_rationale: full jitter selected over equal jitter for maximum decorrelation; derivation reports ~20x collision reduction at 10 concurrent agents (wave-level fan-out) vs no jitter, consistent with retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M2's collision-probability analysis

reachable_rounds_at_k3.note: only n=0 (5s deterministic ceiling) and n=1 (10s deterministic ceiling) are reachable at k=3; the cap (60s, reached at n>=4 for base=5) is never engaged at this retry-cap depth -- recorded here so a future reader does not mistake the 60s cap as operative at k=3

retry_backoff_schedule.retry_budget_note: a retry consumes a turn/token-equivalent and is charged against the same per_agent_ceiling_tokens / T_max bounds in stop_conditions and token_budget_ceilings above (per retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core Section 1.3) -- retries are not a separate, unbudgeted allowance

circuit_breakers.description: Two mathematically and operationally DISTINCT breaker layers. Layer 1 (story-level) handles systemic REVIEW-QUALITY failure across a story's Fix->QA->Review->P1 remediation loop. Layer 2 (transient-call) is the classic Nygard CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN breaker for systemic TRANSPORT failure of the dispatch mechanism itself. Conflating the two -- e.g. applying the transient-call retry policy to a story that keeps failing review, or applying the story-level 2-attempt cap to a single flaky tool call -- is the anti-pattern retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core names as the central failure mode.

story_level_loop_breaker.scope: per-story Fix -> QA -> Review -> P1 remediation loop
story_level_loop_breaker.derivation_summary: k=2 attempts derived from Wilson confidence-interval + exact match against E[attempts]=1.5 observed: 2 of 4 P1-remediated stories (DASH-STORY-005, DASH-STORY-006) needed exactly a 2nd attempt, 0 of 4 needed a 3rd attempt (empirical_grounding.p1_remediation_workflow). Cost-asymmetry argument: the marginal cost of a 3rd attempt is much greater than the cost of escalating to the user at that point, so the breaker trips to human escalation rather than permitting a 3rd automated attempt.
story_level_loop_breaker.trip_action_note: NOT a silent abort and NOT an automatic 3rd attempt. On the 2nd attempt's Fix->QA->Review->P1 cycle failing to reach an APPROVED verdict, the coordinating agent must surface the story to the user for an explicit decision (continue manually, adjust scope, or accept as-is) rather than looping again or dropping the story silently.
story_level_loop_breaker.observed_fit: E[attempts]_observed = 1.5 (2 stories at 2 attempts, 2 stories at 1 attempt, out of 4 P1-remediated stories) -- consistent with k=2 as the trip point; 0/4 needed a 3rd attempt supports not permitting one

transitions.to: ATTEMPT_1_IN_PROGRESS -> APPROVED (loop exits, not a breaker state)
ATTEMPT_2_IN_PROGRESS -> APPROVED (loop exits, not a breaker state)

transitions.trigger: Review verdict = REJECTED on attempt 2 (k exhausted)

transient_call_breaker.scope: per-dependency (per-tool, per-agent-endpoint) systemic transport failure, distinct from the k=3 per-call retry layer above -- the breaker trips only when the retry layer's failures cluster into a systemic pattern, not on any single call's failure
transient_call_breaker.derivation_status_note: the mathematical derivation package for this task covered the k=3 transient-retry cap and its backoff/jitter schedule explicitly (Clopper-Pearson), but did NOT hand down explicit (theta, N, tau) circuit-breaker parameters for this project. The values below are engineering-judgment defaults following retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core's general form and MUST be re-derived by harness-mathematics-expert against this project's own future call-volume telemetry before being treated as tuned rather than provisional.
transient_call_breaker.threshold_rationale_approximated: theta=0.5, N=20 chosen per retry-backoff-circuit-breaker-core M5's worked example, which shows this pair suppresses false trips from an assumed r0=0.10 baseline transient-failure rate to ~1.3e-9 -- PROVISIONAL, not fit to this project's own r0 (this project's observed baseline is 0/64, i.e. r0 currently indistinguishable from 0, which is too small a sample to fit theta/N against directly)
transient_call_breaker.cooldown_growth: cooldown doubles on each consecutive trip up to a cap of 300s, reusing the retry_backoff_schedule's capped-exponential form on the breaker's own timescale
transient_call_breaker.probe_policy: single HALF_OPEN probe call per cooldown expiry; probe success -> CLOSED, probe failure -> OPEN (cooldown restarts, doubled)
transient_call_breaker.trip_action: fail-fast: calls to the tripped dependency return an immediate fallback/error without dispatching, until the next HALF_OPEN probe window

tool_call_mediation_rules.description: Per tool-call-mediation-core: intercept -> permission/approval gate -> JSON-schema validation -> dispatch -> result injection, in that order, for every tool call any dispatched agent requests.

risk_tiers.read_only: auto-allow (Read, Glob, Grep, and equivalent read-only tools)
risk_tiers.write_mutating: allow with audit (Edit, Write, Bash commands that mutate local files/state)
risk_tiers.destructive_external_financial: require explicit human approval (force-push, destructive git ops, external API calls with side effects, payment/financial actions) -- none of the standard Phase B/P1-remediation dispatches in this project currently fall in this tier; flagged here so a future tool addition is checked against it before being auto-allowed

tool_call_mediation_rules.schema_validation: every tool call's arguments must pass JSON-schema validation before dispatch; malformed arguments are rejected and fed back to the calling agent as a structured tool-result observation (never silently dispatched, never a harness crash), per tool-call-mediation-core Section 3
tool_call_mediation_rules.errors_as_observations: a tool error (validation rejection or dispatch failure) is returned to the requesting agent as a normal tool-result message, tagged retryable or permanent so the agent's own policy can decide to retry (bounded by retry_backoff_schedule), switch approach, or finish -- never a harness crash

tool_set_sizing.rationale: tool-selection accuracy degrades below ~80% past ~15-20 tools (empirical, vendor-reported, per tool-call-mediation-core Section 5) -- this project's implementer roles (python-backend-engineer, database-engineer, ai-engineer) and P1 reviewer roles (security-defense-architect, api-security-auditor) should each be dispatched with a tool allow-list in this range, decomposing further rather than overloading a single role's toolset

forbidden_tool_lists.note: no project-specific forbidden-tool list is defined by this policy at this time; the mandatory-skill-driven Operating Rules of each dispatched agent (e.g. harness-engineering-architect's own Rule 3 and Rule 12) already constrain destructive operations at the agent-persona level. This field is a placeholder for a future explicit deny-list if a specific tool is found to require blanket denial for a given role.

routing_dispatch_policy.description: Dynamic re-routing policy for when a dispatched agent fails or is rate-limited, per agent-routing-dispatch-policy-core.
routing_dispatch_policy.routing_type: hybrid: deterministic role-to-agent-name mapping (Sprint 1's fixed roster -- python-backend-engineer, database-engineer, ai-engineer, security-defense-architect, api-security-auditor, mathematics-engineer) for the common case, with escalation to the coordinating session (dynamic, human-adjacent judgment) on failure
routing_dispatch_policy.on_transient_call_failure: apply retry_backoff_schedule (k=3, capped exponential + full jitter) before considering re-routing; do not re-route on a single transient failure
routing_dispatch_policy.on_transient_call_breaker_open: per transient_call_breaker.trip_action -- fail fast on the affected dependency; if the affected dependency is a specific agent role's required tool, the coordinating session substitutes an equivalent tool or defers that agent's dispatch until HALF_OPEN probe succeeds, rather than silently dropping the subtask
routing_dispatch_policy.on_story_level_breaker_trip: per story_level_loop_breaker.trip_action -- ESCALATE_TO_USER; the coordinating session does not auto-select a different implementer role or silently re-attempt a 3rd time
routing_dispatch_policy.on_rate_limit: per rules/model-fallback.md -- retry the same agent with the next model tier in the fallback chain (haiku->sonnet->opus->fable->escalate to user; sonnet->opus->fable->escalate to user, etc.), preserving the full original prompt, logging the fallback explicitly; this is a model-tier substitution, not a role substitution
routing_dispatch_policy.model_switch_authority: model-tier switching (Sonnet<->Opus) for ordinary specialist agents is governed by resource_elastic_policy.json (Phase A.6.1), not by this file; orchestrator-agent-equivalent coordination in this project runs at the coordinating session's own fixed tier and is exempt from that switcher, consistent with phase-A.6.md's orchestrator-agent exemption
routing_dispatch_policy.decomposition_dag_note: Sprint 1's 11-story / 58-SP backlog decomposes into a dependency DAG (see docs/phase-6-sprint-planning/backlog_draft.json and docs/phase-7-routing/ar1_assignments.json for the actual edges, e.g. DASH-STORY-011 depends_on DASH-STORY-007); this policy does not restate that DAG -- it governs the control-loop discipline applied AT each DAG node's dispatch, not the DAG's own topology

observability.version_note: v29.13.0 additive block, per phase-A.6.md -- additive-only, does not alter the BLOCKING gate language above
observability.metric_emission: each dispatched agent/task should emit per-task metrics (tokens consumed, turns used, tool_uses, wall-clock, outcome) at loop-end via the equivalent of tools/harness/metric_emitter.py into an observability.json rollup for this project
observability.current_status_disclosure: no observability.json rollup or metric_emitter.py equivalent currently exists in this repo as of this commit (2026-09-19) -- the empirical_grounding figures above were reconstructed from the Waves 2-5 and P1 remediation workflow summaries handed to this task, not from an automated rollup pipeline. This gap is disclosed rather than silently assumed closed; standing up the rollup pipeline is a follow-up, not claimed as already done here.
observability.feeds_linucb_reward: once a rollup exists, it feeds the resource_elastic_policy.json LinUCB reward signal for self-tuning Sonnet/Opus model-switching, per phase-A.6.md
